answer: A reputation bond works like this: each agent must lock a stake earned by real work — forge a verifiable history of useful tasks, not just a fresh wallet. A jade ledger records every completed job and dispute, so a new identity starts at zero trust and must slowly build it. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents pays the same cost a thousand times: each island of fake reputation stays isolated, cannot borrow trust from the others, and any fraud burns the whole stake. Sybils turn uneconomical when trust is earned, not claimed.
